title.zh: 车轮为什么是圆的
title.en: Why Are Wheels Round?

content.zh: 圆形的轮子滚起来，中心到地面的距离一直不变，所以坐在车里很平稳。如果轮子是方的，每转一下车身就会"咯噔"一下颠起来。
content.en: A round wheel stays the same height as it rolls, so the ride is smooth. A square wheel would bump up and down with every turn.

title.zh: 蜂巢为什么是六边形的
title.en: Why Are Honeycombs Hexagonal?

content.zh: 六边形能一个挨一个紧紧排在一起，中间不留缝，用的蜂蜡也最少。蜜蜂用最少的材料，做出了最结实又最大的家。
content.en: Hexagons fit together with no gaps and need the least wax. Bees use the least material to build the strongest, roomiest home.

title.zh: 井盖为什么是圆的
title.en: Why Are Manhole Covers Round?

content.zh: 圆形的盖子不管怎么转，都不会从井口掉下去——圆的每个方向都一样宽。方的盖子斜着立起来，就能顺着对角线掉进井里。
content.en: A round lid can never fall through, because a circle is the same width every way. A square lid could slip through its own diagonal.

title.zh: 数字 0 是怎么来的
title.en: Where Did Zero Come From?

content.zh: 古人在记账时发现，如果哪一位上一个东西也没有，就空着，容易看错。后来他们画一个圈表示"这里什么都没有"，这就是 0。
content.en: Long ago people left an empty space when a column had nothing in it, which caused mistakes. They began drawing a circle to mean "nothing here" — that is zero.

title.zh: 我们为什么用十根手指头数数
title.en: Why Do We Count in Tens?

content.zh: 因为人有十根手指，数东西时最方便的工具就是自己的手。全世界大多数地方都用"满十就进一位"的办法，这叫十进制。
content.en: We have ten fingers, and hands are the handiest counting tool. Most of the world counts in tens, which we call the decimal system.

title.zh: 时钟上为什么是 12 个数
title.en: Why Do Clocks Have 12 Numbers?

content.zh: 古埃及人喜欢用 12 来分东西，因为 12 能被 2、3、4、6 整除，分起来很方便。他们把白天和黑夜各分成 12 份，钟表也就跟着写 12 个数。
content.en: The ancient Egyptians liked 12 because it divides evenly by 2, 3, 4 and 6. They split day and night into 12 parts each, and clocks kept the number.

title.zh: 金字塔为什么是三角形的
title.en: Why Are Pyramids Triangular?

content.zh: 三角形是最不容易变形的形状，三条边一固定，形状就再也改不了。金字塔做成三角形，几千年来一直稳稳地立着。
content.en: A triangle is the shape that cannot be pushed out of form — once its three sides are set, it will not change. That is why pyramids still stand after thousands of years.

title.zh: 桥上为什么有那么多三角形
title.en: Why Do Bridges Have So Many Triangles?

content.zh: 桥要托住很重的东西，工程师就把许多铁条搭成一个个小三角形。三角形不会变形，桥就变得又轻又结实。
content.en: Bridges must carry heavy loads, so engineers join bars into many small triangles. Triangles do not change shape, making the bridge light and strong.

title.zh: 一年为什么有 12 个月
title.en: Why Does a Year Have 12 Months?

content.zh: 月亮圆缺一回大约要 29 天半，这样的"一个月"过 12 回，正好差不多是一年。后来人们把每月的天数调成 30 或 31 天，凑成一整年。
content.en: The moon takes about 29 and a half days to go from full to full. Twelve of those months make roughly one year, so people set months at 30 or 31 days.

title.zh: 切蛋糕为什么要先分成几等份
title.en: Why Do We Cut a Cake into Equal Pieces?

content.zh: 分成一样大的几份，每个人拿到的才一样多，这才公平。分成 2 份、4 份、8 份最好分，因为它们都能再对半切开。
content.en: Cutting a cake into equal pieces means everyone gets the same amount, which is fair. Halves, quarters and eighths are easiest, since each can be halved again.

title.zh: 七巧板为什么能拼出那么多形状
title.en: Why Can Tangram Make So Many Shapes?

content.zh: 七巧板只有 7 块，但每块的边和角都能和别的块对上。换一换位置，同样的 7 块就能变成房子、小船、小猫。
content.en: Tangram has only seven pieces, yet their edges and corners match each other. Move them around and the same seven pieces become a house, a boat, or a cat.

title.zh: 量东西为什么要用尺子
title.en: Why Do We Measure with a Ruler?

content.zh: 用手量、用脚量，每个人的手和脚都不一样大，量出来的数就对不上。大家约好一个一样长的"1 厘米"，量出来的数才能互相比较。
content.en: Hands and feet are different sizes, so they give different answers. People agreed on one fixed length, the centimetre, so measurements can be compared.

title.zh: 钟表指针为什么顺时针转
title.en: Why Do Clock Hands Turn Clockwise?

content.zh: 最早的钟表是照着日晷做的：在北半球，太阳的影子一天里从左往右、顺着钟表的方向走，指针的方向就这么定了下来。
content.en: Clocks copied the sundial. In the northern hemisphere a shadow sweeps the same way the hands move, so that direction became the standard.

title.zh: 超市价格为什么常以 9 结尾
title.en: Why Do Prices Often End in 9?

content.zh: 9.9 元看着比 10 元“少一个整数”，我们会觉得便宜不少，其实只差一毛钱。这是商家玩的数字小把戏。
content.en: 9.9 looks much cheaper than 10, even though it is only a tiny bit less. Shops use this trick because our eyes read the first digit first.

title.zh: 骰子相对的两面加起来为什么都是 7
title.en: Why Do Opposite Dice Faces Add Up to 7?

content.zh: 骰子上 1 对 6、2 对 5、3 对 4，相对的两面点数和都是 7。这样点数分布才均匀，掷起来才公平。
content.en: On a die, 1 sits opposite 6, 2 opposite 5, and 3 opposite 4. Every pair adds up to 7, so the dots are spread evenly and the die stays fair.

title.zh: 扑克牌为什么有 54 张
title.en: Why Does a Deck Have 54 Cards?

content.zh: 52 张是一年 52 周的化身：四种花色代表春夏秋冬，每种 13 张是一季的周数。另外两张大小王是后来加进去的。
content.en: The 52 cards stand for the 52 weeks of a year: four suits for the four seasons, 13 cards each for the weeks in a season. The two jokers were added later.

title.zh: 棋盘为什么是 64 个格
title.en: Why Does a Chessboard Have 64 Squares?

content.zh: 国际象棋棋盘是 8 乘 8，一共 64 格，黑白相间。64 是个平方数，横竖都对称，摆起棋子来很整齐。
content.en: A chessboard is 8 by 8, so it has 64 squares in two colours. 64 is a square number, which makes the board neat and balanced in every direction.

title.zh: 量角器为什么是半圆的
title.en: Why Is a Protractor Half a Circle?

content.zh: 一个整圆是 360 度，半圆就是 180 度。平时要量的角大多不超过 180 度，做成半圆既够用又省材料。
content.en: A full circle is 360 degrees, so half a circle is 180. Most angles we measure are smaller than that, and a half circle is cheaper to make.

title.zh: 圆周率为什么约等于 3.14
title.en: Why Is Pi About 3.14?

content.zh: 拿任何一个圆的周长除以它的直径，得到的数都一样，大约是 3.14。这个永远除不尽、也不循环的数就叫圆周率。
content.en: Divide any circle's rim by its width and you always get the same number, about 3.14. This number never ends and never repeats, and it is called pi.

title.zh: 足球为什么用五边形和六边形拼成
title.en: Why Is a Football Made of Pentagons and Hexagons?

content.zh: 12 块黑五边形和 20 块白六边形拼在一起，正好围出一个接近圆球的形状，踢起来滚得又稳又远。
content.en: 12 black pentagons and 20 white hexagons fit together into a shape very close to a sphere, so the ball rolls straight and true.

title.zh: 为什么两点之间直线最短
title.en: Why Is a Straight Line the Shortest Path?

content.zh: 在平地上，从一点到另一点拉直那条线最短；绕弯的路可以看成许多小段拼起来的，总比直的那条长。
content.en: On flat ground the straight path is shortest. Any curved path can be split into little straight pieces, and together they are always longer.

title.zh: 为什么要背乘法表
title.en: Why Do We Learn the Times Table?

content.zh: 乘法是“几个几相加”的快办法。把九九表记熟，算 7 乘 8 就不用数七遍八，买东西、分东西都快得多。
content.en: Multiplication is a shortcut for adding the same number many times. Knowing the table means you get 7 times 8 at once instead of counting eight seven times.

title.zh: 钟表为什么有三根指针
title.en: Why Does a Clock Have Three Hands?

content.zh: 时针走得最慢，管几点；分针快一些，管几分；秒针最快，管几秒。三根各管一样，时间才读得准。
content.en: The short hour hand shows the hour, the long minute hand shows minutes, and the thin second hand shows seconds. Each hand does one job.

title.zh: 为什么一打是 12 个
title.en: Why Is a Dozen Twelve?

content.zh: 12 能被 2、3、4、6 整除，分起来最方便。古人常用它数鸡蛋、数月份，后来就成了“一打”。
content.en: Twelve can be split evenly by 2, 3, 4 and 6, which makes sharing easy. People counted eggs and months this way, and a dozen was born.

title.zh: 为什么一小时是 60 分钟
title.en: Why Is an Hour 60 Minutes?

content.zh: 古巴比伦人喜欢用 60 来数数，因为它能被 2、3、4、5、6 整除，分起来最方便。这个习惯就一直用到今天。
content.en: The Babylonians counted in 60s because 60 divides neatly by 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, and the habit has stayed with us ever since.

title.zh: 为什么每四年要多出一天
title.en: Why Do We Add a Day Every Four Years?

content.zh: 地球绕太阳一圈其实是 365 天零 6 小时。攒四年就多出差不多一整天，补在 2 月 29 日，这一年叫闰年。
content.en: Earth takes 365 days and about 6 hours to circle the sun. After four years that adds up to a whole day, added on 29 February in a leap year.

title.zh: 为什么一个月有时 30 天有时 31 天
title.en: Why Are Some Months 30 Days and Some 31?

content.zh: 古罗马的日历几经改动，留下的月份长短不齐。2 月最少，后来又把闰日加在它身上。
content.en: The Roman calendar was changed several times, leaving months of different lengths. February ended up shortest, and the leap day goes to it.

title.zh: 为什么大数要每隔三位加个逗号
title.en: Why Do Big Numbers Have Commas?

content.zh: 从右往左每三位加一个逗号，正好对着千、百万、十亿，一眼就能看出这个数有多大。
content.en: A comma every three digits lines up with thousands, millions and billions, so you can judge the size of a number at a glance.

title.zh: 为什么不能除以 0
title.en: Why Can't You Divide by Zero?

content.zh: 除法是看能分成几份。分成 0 份没有意义，而且怎么分都对不上原来的数，所以数学家规定不能除。
content.en: Division asks how many equal groups you can make. Zero groups makes no sense and no answer works, so mathematicians forbid it.

title.zh: 为什么要先算乘除后算加减
title.en: Why Do We Multiply Before We Add?

content.zh: 乘除是几个几的简写，比加减更紧密。大家统一先算乘除，同一道算式才只有一个答案。
content.en: Multiplication is shorthand for repeated adding, so it binds more tightly. Agreeing to do it first means every sum has one answer.

title.zh: 为什么要学负数
title.en: Why Do We Learn Negative Numbers?

content.zh: 负数表示比 0 还少：零下的温度、欠的钱、海平面以下的深度。没有它，这些就说不清楚。
content.en: Negative numbers show less than zero: temperatures below freezing, money owed, or ground below sea level. Without them these are hard to describe.

title.zh: 为什么要先估一估
title.en: Why Should We Estimate First?

content.zh: 算之前先估个大概，能立刻发现算错没有。买东西时估一估，也知道带的钱够不够。
content.en: Estimating first lets you spot a wrong answer at once. It also tells you whether you have enough money before you reach the till.

title.zh: 平均数有什么用
title.en: What Is an Average For?

content.zh: 把一组数加起来再平分，得到一个代表大家的数。看平均分比盯着每一次成绩更容易看出整体水平。
content.en: Add a set of numbers and share them out evenly and you get one number standing for the group, so the overall level shows at a glance.

title.zh: 为什么要画统计图
title.en: Why Do We Draw Charts?

content.zh: 图能把一堆数字变成看得见的高低长短，谁多谁少、是升是降，一眼就看明白。
content.en: A chart turns rows of numbers into bars and lines you can see, so which is biggest and which way things are moving is obvious.

title.zh: 百分数是什么意思
title.en: What Does Percent Mean?

content.zh: 百分数就是把总数分成 100 份来看。考了 85%，就是说 100 分里拿到了 85 分。
content.en: Percent means out of every hundred. Score 85 percent and you got 85 out of 100.

title.zh: 为什么三角形三个角加起来是 180 度
title.en: Why Do a Triangle's Angles Add Up to 180°?

content.zh: 把三角形的三个角剪下来拼在一起，正好排成一条直线，也就是 180 度。
content.en: Cut out the three corners of a triangle and put them together: they form a straight line, which is 180 degrees.

title.zh: 为什么平行线永远不会相交
title.en: Why Do Parallel Lines Never Meet?

content.zh: 平行线之间的距离处处相等，方向也一模一样，所以不管画多长都不会碰头。
content.en: Parallel lines keep exactly the same gap and the same direction, so however far you draw them they never touch.

title.zh: 为什么周长一样面积可以不一样
title.en: Why Can Shapes with the Same Perimeter Have Different Areas?

content.zh: 同样长的绳子围成不同的形状，装下的地方不一样大。围得越圆，装下的面积越大。
content.en: The same length of string can enclose different amounts of space, and the closer the shape is to a circle, the more it holds.

title.zh: 体积和容积有什么不一样
title.en: What Is the Difference Between Volume and Capacity?

content.zh: 体积是物体自己占了多大地方，容积是里面能装多少东西。同一个杯子，外面看和里面量不一样。
content.en: Volume is the space an object takes up; capacity is how much it can hold. The same cup measures differently outside and in.

title.zh: 什么是对称
title.en: What Is Symmetry?

content.zh: 一个图形对折后两边完全重合，就是对称。蝴蝶的翅膀、人的脸，都藏着这条看不见的折痕。
content.en: A shape is symmetrical if both halves match when it is folded, and butterfly wings and human faces both hide that invisible fold.

title.zh: 为什么一张纸对折几次就折不动了
title.en: Why Can't You Fold Paper Many Times?

content.zh: 每折一次厚度就翻一倍，折 7 次已经是 128 层，比一本书还厚，再折就折不动了。
content.en: Each fold doubles the thickness, so after seven folds you have 128 layers, thicker than a book, and it will not bend any more.

title.zh: 什么是黄金比例
title.en: What Is the Golden Ratio?

content.zh: 把一个东西按大约 1 比 1.618 分开，看上去特别舒服。这个比例在贝壳、花瓣和名画里都能找到。
content.en: Split something roughly 1 to 1.618 and it looks just right, and you find this ratio in shells, petals and famous paintings.

title.zh: 莫比乌斯带是什么
title.en: What Is a Möbius Strip?

content.zh: 把纸带扭半圈再把两头粘起来，就成了一个只有一面、一条边的圈。沿着中间画下去，能一直画回起点。
content.en: Twist a paper strip half a turn and glue the ends together and you get a band with one side and one edge, so drawing along the middle brings you back to the start.

title.zh: 九宫格里的数字有什么秘密
title.en: What Is the Secret of the Magic Square?

content.zh: 把 1 到 9 填进九宫格，让横、竖、斜三格相加都等于 15，这就成了幻方。古人觉得它很神奇。
content.en: Put 1 to 9 in a 3 by 3 grid so every row, column and diagonal adds to 15. That is a magic square, and people once thought it magical.

title.zh: 三件衣服能搭配出几种穿法
title.en: How Many Outfits Do Three Clothes Make?

content.zh: 3 件上衣配 2 条裤子就是 3 乘 2 等于 6 种。每多一样选择，搭配数就成倍增长。
content.en: Three tops with two pairs of trousers give 3 times 2, or 6 outfits, and every extra choice multiplies the number of combinations.

title.zh: 抛硬币真是正反各一半吗
title.en: Is a Coin Toss Really 50-50?

content.zh: 理论上正反各一半，但抛的次数少时常常一边倒。抛得越多，两边才会越来越接近一半。
content.en: In theory both sides come up equally, but over few tosses one side often leads, and the more you toss the closer it gets to half and half.

title.zh: 为什么排队时总觉得自己那队最慢
title.en: Why Does Your Queue Always Seem Slowest?

content.zh: 旁边的队伍往前动你会注意到，不动的时候你不看。记住的多是别人前进的画面，就觉得自己的慢。
content.en: You notice other queues when they move and ignore them when they do not, so you remember the moving moments and yours feels slower.

title.zh: 为什么算盘能算得那么快
title.en: Why Is an Abacus So Fast?

content.zh: 算盘用珠子的位置表示数字，手指一拨就是一次加减。熟练的人拨珠比按计算器还快。
content.en: An abacus shows numbers by the position of beads, and one flick of a finger is one sum, so a skilled user can beat a calculator.

title.zh: 阿拉伯数字是怎么传到全世界的
title.en: How Did Arabic Numerals Spread?

content.zh: 这套数字是印度人发明的，经阿拉伯商人带进欧洲，因为好写好算就传开了，所以叫阿拉伯数字。
content.en: These numerals were invented in India and carried to Europe by Arab traders, and being easy to write and reckon with they spread everywhere.

title.zh: 一米到底有多长
title.en: How Long Is a Metre Exactly?

content.zh: 最早把地球从赤道到北极的一千万分之一定为 1 米。后来科学家改用光在真空中跑过的距离来定义。
content.en: A metre was first set as one ten-millionth of the way from the equator to the pole, and today scientists define it by the distance light travels.

title.zh: 秤是怎么称出重量的
title.en: How Does a Scale Weigh Things?

content.zh: 东西压上去弹簧就被压短，压得越重缩得越多，指针就指到更大的数。电子秤则是把压力变成电信号。
content.en: Weight presses a spring shorter, and the heavier the load the further the pointer moves, while electronic scales turn the push into an electrical signal.

title.zh: 为什么尺子上要分厘米和毫米
title.en: Why Are Rulers Marked in Centimetres and Millimetres?

content.zh: 大格数起来快，小格量得准。先读厘米再数毫米，又省事又精确。
content.en: Big marks are quick to count and small marks are accurate, so read the centimetres first and then the millimetres.

title.zh: 为什么要进位
title.en: Why Do We Carry in Addition?

content.zh: 一位上满了 10 就装不下，只好把 10 个一合成 1 个十送到前一位。这就是进位。
content.en: When a column reaches ten it is full, so ten ones become one ten and move to the next column, and that is carrying.

title.zh: 条形码是怎么读出商品的
title.en: How Does a Barcode Tell You the Product?

content.zh: 粗细不同的黑白条纹代表不同的数字，扫码器读出这组数字，再从电脑里查出这件商品的名字和价格。
content.en: Stripes of different widths stand for digits, and the scanner reads them and the computer looks up the name and price.

title.zh: 影子怎么能量出金字塔的高度
title.en: How Can a Shadow Measure a Pyramid?

content.zh: 同一时刻，物体的影长和身高成同样的比例。量出影子和自己的身高，就能算出金字塔有多高。
content.en: At the same moment shadow length and height keep the same ratio, so measure your own height and shadow and you can work out the pyramid's height.

title.zh: 走迷宫有什么窍门
title.en: Is There a Trick for Solving Mazes?

content.zh: 一直贴着一边墙走，手不离墙，迟早能走到出口。这个办法叫贴墙法，不会在岔路里打转。
content.en: Keep one hand on the same wall and keep walking and sooner or later you reach the exit, because this wall-follower rule keeps you from going in circles.

title.zh: 数独为什么不能重复
title.en: Why Can't Numbers Repeat in Sudoku?

content.zh: 数独要求每行、每列、每宫里 1 到 9 各出现一次。不能重复正是它唯一的规则，也是难点。
content.en: Sudoku asks that 1 to 9 appear once in every row, column and block, and no repeats is the only rule and the whole challenge.

title.zh: 为什么有的除法永远除不完
title.en: Why Do Some Divisions Never End?

content.zh: 像 1 除以 3 得到 0.3333，小数部分会一直重复下去。这样的数叫循环小数，写也写不完。
content.en: One divided by three gives 0.3333 with the threes going on forever, and such numbers are called recurring decimals and never finish.

title.zh: 地图上的比例尺有什么用
title.en: What Is a Map's Scale For?

content.zh: 比例尺告诉你图上 1 厘米代表实际多远。有了它，量一量地图就能算出两地的真实距离。
content.en: The scale tells you how far one centimetre on paper stands for in real life, so you can measure the map and get the true distance.

title.zh: 为什么大包装不一定更便宜
title.en: Why Isn't the Big Pack Always Cheaper?

content.zh: 要看的是单价，也就是每 100 克多少钱。把总价除以重量比一比，才知道哪个真正划算。
content.en: What matters is the unit price, the cost per 100 grams, so divide the price by the weight and compare before you buy.
